section: New initiatives, programmes and achievements in India's renewable energy sector
subsections: Global initiatives led by India → purpose

accepted.s:
With reference to the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, consider the following statements:
1. It is a Central Sector scheme for the period 2024 to 2026-27.
2. It aims to cover one crore rooftop households.
3. It provides free power up to 300 units per month.
4. It envisages addition of 30 GW of rooftop solar capacity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana is a Central Sector scheme for 2024-2026-27. It targets one crore rooftop households, free power up to 300 units per month and 30 GW of rooftop solar capacity.
accepted.tq: Use the complete-all-statements option when every numerical and descriptive detail is correct.

accepted.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, approximately how much rooftop solar capacity had been added under the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana?
accepted.x: The Economic Survey 2025-26 reports approximately 8 GW of rooftop solar capacity added under the scheme.
accepted.tq: Separate the latest achievement figure from the scheme’s overall target.

accepted.s: PM-KUSUM is primarily associated with:
accepted.x: PM-KUSUM focuses on the solarisation of agricultural power use, including standalone solar pumps and grid-connected agricultural pumps.
accepted.tq: Match the programme with its sector-specific objective.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the figures reported for PM-KUSUM in the Economic Survey 2025-26?
o: 9.75 lakh standalone solar pumps under Component B and 11,781 grid pumps solarised under Component C
30 lakh standalone solar pumps under Component B and 8,000 grid pumps under Component C
9.75 lakh grid pumps under Component B and 11,781 standalone solar pumps under Component C
11,781 standalone solar pumps under Component B and 9.75 lakh grid pumps under Component C
accepted.x: PM-KUSUM reported 9.75 lakh standalone solar pumps under Component B and 11,781 grid pumps solarised under Component C.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the component labels and their associated numerical figures.

accepted.s: The Green Term Ahead Market (GTAM) is best described as:
o: A renewable-energy-only trading segment on the Indian Energy Exchange
A carbon-tax market operated by the Reserve Bank of India
A bilateral market for nuclear power operated by SECI
A coal-only trading segment regulated by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
accepted.x: GTAM is a renewable-energy-only trading segment on the Indian Energy Exchange (IEX), launched in 2020.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact market segment and the institution associated with it.

accepted.s:
With reference to the Indian Energy Exchange (IEX), consider the following statements:
1. It was established in 2008.
2. It is regulated by the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission.
3. It trades in Day Ahead Market, Term Ahead Market, renewable energy and ESCerts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: IEX was established in 2008, is regulated by CERC, and trades DAM, TAM, renewable energy and ESCerts.
accepted.tq: Combine institutional identity, regulatory authority and functions in one statement set.

accepted.s: The PM Surya Sarovar Yojana, approved in July 2026, has an outlay of:
accepted.x: The Cabinet-approved PM Surya Sarovar Yojana has an outlay of ₹5,070 crore.
accepted.tq: Distinguish scheme outlays from nearby project investment figures.

accepted.s: The principal target of the PM Surya Sarovar Yojana is to develop:
o: 30 GW of rooftop solar capacity by 2030
5,000 MW of floating solar capacity by 2030-31
100 GW of solar module manufacturing capacity by 2026
accepted.x: The scheme targets 5,000 MW of floating solar capacity by 2030-31.
accepted.tq: Link the scheme with its distinctive technology, capacity and deadline.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the PM Surya Sarovar Yojana?
o: CFA up to ₹1 crore per MW — SECI implements the scheme
CFA up to ₹1 lakh per MW — IEX implements the scheme
CFA up to ₹5 crore per MW — CERC implements the scheme
CFA up to ₹30 lakh per MW — MNRE implements the scheme
accepted.x: The PM Surya Sarovar Yojana provides Central Financial Assistance up to ₹1 crore per MW and is implemented by SECI.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure assistance figure and verify the implementing agency.

accepted.s: The International Solar Alliance was established as a joint initiative of:
accepted.x: The International Solar Alliance was jointly initiated by India and France at COP21 in Paris in 2015.
accepted.tq: Use the founding-country pair to distinguish similar international initiatives.
accepted.sec: Global initiatives led by India → purpose

accepted.s: The principal purpose of the International Solar Alliance is to function as a platform for:
accepted.x: The International Solar Alliance serves as a platform to promote and facilitate solar deployment.
accepted.tq: Identify the initiative from its functional objective rather than its founding event.
accepted.sec: Global initiatives led by India → purpose

accepted.s: One Sun One World One Grid (OSOWOG) refers to:
o: A national coal transmission grid under the Ministry of Coal
A transnational solar grid under the International Solar Alliance
A biofuel blending programme under the Global Biofuels Alliance
A global wind-purchasing platform operated by IREDA
accepted.x: OSOWOG is a transnational solar grid concept under the International Solar Alliance. Its roadmap was operationalised at the 8th ISA Assembly in 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the grid concept from other renewable-energy programmes by its transnational scope.
accepted.sec: Global initiatives led by India → purpose

accepted.s: The Green Grids Initiative-OSOWOG was launched by India and the United Kingdom at:
o: The G20 Summit, New Delhi, in 2023
The UN Climate Action Summit, in 2019
accepted.x: The Green Grids Initiative-OSOWOG was launched by India and the United Kingdom at COP26 in Glasgow in 2021.
accepted.tq: Use the event-location-year combination to separate related climate initiatives.

accepted.s: As reported on 15 August 2026, India’s approximate installed power capacity and non-fossil share were respectively:
accepted.x: The reported figures were approximately 552 GW of installed capacity and more than 54% from non-fossil sources.
accepted.tq: Keep the latest aggregate figures distinct from earlier and target figures.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents India’s reported renewable capacity figures as of 15 August 2026?
accepted.x: The reported installed capacities were 164.59 GW of solar and 58.14 GW of wind.
accepted.tq: Avoid reversing paired sectoral figures in a comparison question.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India’s target is to achieve 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030.
2. The COP26 Panchamrit goal of 50% non-fossil capacity by 2030 was reported as having been achieved five years early.
3. The non-fossil share was reported as 51.93% by December 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: India has a 500 GW non-fossil capacity target for 2030; the 50% Panchamrit capacity goal was reported as achieved five years early, and the share was 51.93% by December 2025.
accepted.tq: Separate a long-term capacity target from an already-reported milestone and percentage.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the reported wind-energy targets?
accepted.x: The reported wind-energy targets are 100 GW by 2030 and 155 GW by 2035.
accepted.tq: Check the order of milestones before selecting the numerical pair.

accepted.s: India’s solar module manufacturing capacity was reported as approximately how much in March 2026?
accepted.x: Solar module manufacturing capacity was reported as approximately 172 GW in March 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish manufacturing capacity from installed generation capacity.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about India’s energy mix and power subsidies is correct?
o: Coal accounts for less than 20% of primary energy and States spend ₹5,070 crore annually on subsidies.
Coal accounts for more than 70% of primary energy and States spend ₹2.4 lakh crore monthly on subsidies.
Coal accounts for about 55% of primary energy and more than 70% of generation; States spend about ₹2.4 lakh crore annually on power subsidies.
Coal accounts for about 55% of generation and States spend ₹5,750 crore annually on subsidies.
accepted.x: Coal still accounts for approximately 55% of primary energy and more than 70% of electricity generation. States spend around ₹2.4 lakh crore per year on power subsidies.
accepted.tq: Check both the energy-share basis and the time unit attached to the subsidy figure.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding renewable-energy initiatives in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Tata Renewable has a planned 800 MW hybrid project involving an investment of ₹5,750 crore.
2. A solar Centre of Excellence is associated with IIT Tirupati and the University of New South Wales.
3. The reported hybrid project is a 5,000 MW floating solar project implemented by SECI.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh-related initiatives include Tata Renewable’s 800 MW hybrid project costing ₹5,750 crore and a solar Centre of Excellence with IIT Tirupati and UNSW. Statement 3 describes the PM Surya Sarovar target, not the Tata Renewable project.
accepted.tq: Separate the State-specific project from a similarly worded national scheme.
